claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is in bulk powder form.
The as-deposited alloy has a relatively coarse grain structure.
High-pressure torsion followed by annealing will produce ultrafine grain boundaries and a refined subgrain structure.
Grain refinement will increase the density of nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transformation.
Distributed nucleation sites will lower the energy barriers for the magnetostructural transformation.
Lower transformation barriers will mitigate the abruptness of the first-order transition.
Mitigating the abrupt first-order transition will reduce hysteresis.
The processed alloy will exhibit a broader, more gradual magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
The processed alloy will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The processed alloy will show improved reproducibility during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The as-deposited baseline shows a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited baseline has significant hysteretic losses.
The predicted behavior should hold for rare-earth-free non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy powders processed under the specified high-pressure-torsion and annealing conditions.
Mechanical stability will be maintained under the proposed processing conditions.
The extent of hysteresis reduction and transition broadening may depend on precise processing conditions and defect formation during severe plastic deformation.
